question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
Employees may opt‑out “within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute.”【621/2025 §33】  

- The provision sets a six‑month deadline for deciding whether to decline the offer.  

**Caveat:** The excerpts give only the time limit; they do not detail the notification procedure or any other conditions for exercising the option.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
A container depot operator must submit the renewal application **at least 30 days before the licence expires**.

- The renewal must be lodged “*not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued*” [657/2025 §6].

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
The amendment permits the notice of dishonour to be given **in writing, by personal communication, by facsimile transmission, or by any other electronic means that sufficiently identify the bill**.  

- “The notice may be given in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means which sufficiently identify the bill…” [601/2025 §8]  
- The same wording appears in the Gazette versions of 2024 and 2025, confirming it applies to the Bills of Exchange Ordinance. [601/2025 §8]  

*Caveat: The excerpt only lists the permitted methods; it does not detail procedural requirements such as timing.*

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
The Society, as a body corporate, may acquire and retain any movable or immovable property that comes to it by purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or any other means, and it may manage that property by **selling, mortgaging, leasing, exchanging or otherwise disposing of it**, subject to other laws and its own rules.  

- Authority to take and hold property — “able and capable in law to take and hold any property, movable or immovable… which may become vested in it by virtue of any purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise”【047/2026 §13】.  
- Power to dispose of property — “with power to sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of the same”【047/2026 §13】.  

*Caveat:* The clause limits these powers to what is permitted by other written law and the Society’s rules under section 7; further management details are not specified in the excerpt.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The amendment deletes the reference to “Container Operators” from the long title, so the Act will be titled **“Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act.”**  

- The words “…freight forwarders, non‑Vessel operating common carriers **and container operators**” are substituted with “…freight forwarders **and non‑Vessel operating common carriers**” [658/2025 §2].  
- Accordingly, “Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers **and Container Operators** Act” becomes “Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders and Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act” [658/2025 §3].

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The legislation is the **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. … of 2026** (introduced as Bill 043/2026 and re‑presented as Bill 055/2026). It incorporates a corporate body – the Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation – to promote national economic growth and rural‑resource development.  

- Short title: “Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. … of 2026” [043/2026 §1].  
- Objects include “contribute to national and social development by developing, promoting, establishing, expanding or modernising all economic sectors in Sri Lanka” and “empower rural, estate and underserved communities” [043/2026 §3].  
- The Act creates the Foundation as a Voluntary Social Service Organization with powers to acquire property, enter contracts, receive donations and run development programmes [043/2026 §2‑§6].

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer: A person who is **over seventy years of age** is disqualified from being appointed as a member of the Authority’s Board【613/2025 §9】.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The body corporate must settle all debts and liabilities that existed **on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of the Act**【009/2026 §12】.  

- “All debts and liabilities of the Trust existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act, shall be paid by the body corporate hereby constituted”【009/2026 §12】.  

*Caveat*: The exact commencement date of the Act is not given in the excerpt, so the specific calendar day cannot be identified from the available text.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The “Director‑General” is defined as **the Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act**【494/2024 §6】.  

- The amendment substitutes “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” with “Director‑General” throughout the principal enactment【595/2025 §2】.  
- All other references to the former titles are read as referring to the Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department【595/2025 §2】.  

*Caveat: The definition is taken from the 2024 amendment, which is reproduced unchanged in later amendments.*

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
The term **“qualified auditor”** means either an individual accountant who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other institute created by law) and holds a practising certificate issued by that institute’s Council, **or** a firm of accountants whose resident partners each satisfy that same membership and certification requirement【172/2022 §10】.  

- Individual: member of ICA Sri Lanka or another statutory institute, with a Council‑issued certificate to practise as an Accountant【172/2022 §10】.  
- Firm: all resident partners are such members and each holds a Council‑issued practising certificate【172/2022 §10】.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
The amendment requires the Commission to **determine the fare formula** and then **publish the resulting fare tables**, after which each operator must **adopt those tables and display the fares on its vehicles**.

- The Commission computes fares “in accordance with the formula determined by the Commission from time to time … adhering to the national policy … and specified by Order published in the Gazette”【577/2025 §19】.  
- It then “publish[es] the lists of the transportation service fares … in the official website of the Commission”【549/2024 §19】.  
- Each transport service provider must “prepare a list of the transportation service fares applicable to his service … and cause such list to be displayed at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle”【577/2025 §19】.  

*Caveat: The provision on inspection (sub‑s (3)) is not a step for setting/showing fares but gives the Commission enforcement powers.*

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
The magistrate must actively monitor any approved detention centre located in his jurisdiction.

- **Monthly unannounced inspection:** He must visit the centre once a month, interview the suspects and review detention registers, orders and other required documents [078/2026 §33 (1)].  
- **Access guarantee:** The centre’s authority must give the magistrate prompt, unimpeded access for these inspections [078/2026 §33 (3)].  
- **Torture response:** If he suspects or is told that a suspect was tortured or subjected to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment, he must order an immediate medical examination and, after hearing the suspect and police, act in accordance with section 31 [078/2026 §33 (4)‑(5)].  

*Caveat: the bill’s text does not detail the exact procedures for “acting in terms of section 31.”*

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
A struck‑off company may seek a court order to be re‑registered and have its assets returned, but the assets are treated as having vested in the State until that order.

- The company can, within 10 years of the amendment’s operation, apply to a court (with the Attorney‑General as a party) to show cause for re‑registration; the court may then “permit the re‑registration of the company and … make an order for the return to the company of all property previously vested in the State”【582/2025 §17】.  
- Until such an order, the former assets “vest in and be at the disposal of the State”【582/2025 §17】.  
- If the State has already dealt with the property, “the rights of third parties who have acquired such rights … in good faith shall not be affected” and, where the property was destroyed, damaged, or never taken by the State, “the State shall not be liable to any party”【582/2025 §17】.  

**Caveat:** The passage does not explain the fate of the assets if the company does not apply for re‑registration or after the ten‑year period expires.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
A person convicted under the revised Section 23r must pay a fine of **at least ₹100,000 and up to ₹1,000,000**, and if the offence continues after conviction an **additional fine of ₹5,000 for each day** of continuation.  

- Conviction fine: “not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees” [032/2026 §18]  
- Continuing‑offence surcharge: “a fine of five thousand rupees for each day … after conviction” [032/2026 §18]  

*Caveat: the figure reflects the amendment introduced in Bill 032/2026 (identical to 026/2026).*

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The amendment adds **methamphetamine** to the named narcotics and creates a new offence for manufacturing any other dangerous drug in Groups A‑E, punishable by a **fine of ₹200,000‑₹500,000 and/or imprisonment of 10‑20 years** on conviction by a High Court without a jury.

- The words “heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium” are replaced with “heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine” [068/2026 §2].  
- A new paragraph (aa) makes manufacturing any drug in Groups A‑E (except those five) an offence, liable to a fine “not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, or imprisonment … for a period not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years, or both” [068/2026 §2].

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The amendment revises Section 5’s turnover thresholds and the dates they apply:

* Paragraph (b) drops the word **“or”** after “hundred and twenty million rupees” – the 120 million‑rupee limit remains but the wording is simplified【017/2026 §3】.  
* Paragraph (c) changes the 60 million‑rupee limit to apply **“on or after 1 January 2024 and prior to 1 April 2026”** (and adds “or” after the figure)【017/2026 §3】.  
* A new paragraph (d) is inserted: for any period **commencing on or after 1 April 2026**, the aggregate turnover for four consecutive quarters must **not exceed 36 million rupees**【017/2026 §3】.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
The amendment raises the retirement age for some judges from 61 to 63 years and fixes the retirement age for all other judges and magistrates at 62 years, overriding the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance.

- “judges may now serve until 63 instead of 61” [064/2026]  
- “the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be 62 years” [058/2026 §3]

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
The legislation is the **Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. 2025**, introduced as Bill 596/2025 (presented 8 May 2025).  

- The Act “may be cited as the Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Act, No. of 2025” [596/2025 §1].  
- It creates the foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, able to sue, be sued, use a common seal and own property [596/2025 §2].  
- The same Act was published in the Gazette as GS 581/2025 on 10 April 2025 [581/2025].

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act, Bill 059/2026** repeals the Chief of Defence Staff Act No. 35 of 2009, which created the chief‑of‑defence‑staff position.  

- The Act is cited as “Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Act, No. of 2026” [059/2026 §1].  
- Section 2 expressly states: “The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed.” [059/2026 §2].  
- An identical version was published as Gazette Bill 036/2026 on 15 May 2026. [036/2026]  

**Caveat:** Both Bill 059/2026 (presented on 4 Aug 2026) and Gazette Bill 036/2026 contain the same repeal provisions.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Bill — Bill 604/2025** proposes to amend the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016.

- It repeals and substitutes subsection (1) of Section 3 of the 2016 Act to raise the minimum monthly and daily wages [604/2025 §2].  
- The bill’s description states it “amends Section 3 of the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act 2016” [604/2025].  

*Caveat: a Gazette version of the same amendment also appears as Bill 586/2025, but the presented parliamentary bill is 604/2025.*

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The 2025 bill that aimed to modify the 1988 gambling‑tax law is **Bill 642/2025 – Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment) – Bill**, which proposes changes to the Betting and Gaming Levy Act No 40 of 1988.  

- It revises the levy rates (10 % → 15 % → 18 %) and doubles a US $50 charge to US $100 【642/2025】.

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The amendment is **Bill 056/2026 – “Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Act, 2026.”**  

- It amends **Section 7** (and Sections 13 and 20a) of the **Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No 47 of 1956** 【056/2026 §2】.  
- The bill raises the penalty for offences against women, young workers and children from “ten thousand rupees” to “one hundred thousand rupees” 【056/2026 §2】.  
- It is cited as the **Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Act, 2026** 【056/2026 §1】.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 amendment that revises the Strategic Development Projects Act 2008 is **Bill 650/2025 – “Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill”** (presented 14 Nov 2025) 【650/2025】.  

- The same amendment was published earlier as **Bill 643/2025 – Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) – GS** (Gazette 7 Nov 2025) 【643/2025】.  

*Caveat: both bills contain identical text; the Bill 650/2025 version is the formal parliamentary submission.*

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
The **Twenty‑Second Amendment to the Constitution** is proposed in **Bill 065/2026** (presented 18 August 2026) – the 2026 bill that seeks the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution【065/2026】.  

- The bill amends Article 107 (judges’ retirement ages) and Article 137 (maximum number of Supreme Court judges)【065/2026 §2】【065/2026 §3】.  
- A Gazette‑published version of the same amendment appears as **Bill 057/2026** dated 7 August 2026【057/2026】.
